evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Missing entirely. Rep jumps straight to 'before we start on this, I just want to check-in if you have any special instructions or concerns' without framing the 10-15 minute call or securing a yes.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after extensive probing: 'just want to check-in if you have any special instructions or concerns about this move that you want us to discuss on this call?' — but this comes at the very beginning, before logistics details. The concern-check is framed loosely and not properly set up as 'what are your biggest concerns / what do you want answers to on this call?'
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (apartment), floors (4th, both), rooms (one bedroom), walking distances (50 ft from first apt to elevator, 100+ ft for couch to freight elevator, 100 ft at destination), additional items (couch requiring freight elevator), special considerations (elevators across the street, new building not yet visited). Box count: 'less than $10' mentioned but no formal box-count or overflow check.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: 'Are you good with packing? You're planning to handle all the packing yourself or do you need help with that as well?' — Yes, asked.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Not asked in the recognizable form ('typical box count for a home your size is X, do you have anything like china or a book collection'). Rep notes 'less than $10' in boxes but does not probe for overflow or typical box benchmarks.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full anchor and personalization: 'usually one bedroom apartment can take twenty and a half hours to complete. But this accounting for the walking distance for the patch or in the new apartment we can just bump it up a little to four hours. So there's an estimated budget of $900 including the rotation fee already.' Personalized to walking distance and freight elevator complexity.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full disclosure: '$190 per hour... for the two men and the truck, and everything we need, like the taxes, insurance, credit card fees, this assembly, reassembly. That's all in the price.' Also disclosed one-time transportation fee of $140, two and a half hour minimum, fifteen minute intervals, no hidden fees. Also mentioned 'meet your mover' and no daily contractor work.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep moves directly to email and confirmation without asking 'Does that feel fair?' or waiting for customer buy-in on the price.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Full: 'lastly on time guarantee if we run late, we provide discounts for your move again.'
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Partial. Mentioned: 'we will also include our no worries damage coverage which would give you up to $2,000 coverage for any accidental damages' — but does NOT mention 'no deductible / no fine print' framing or explicitly state it's built into the rate (not an add-on). The phrase is brief and lacks the reassurance framing.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or confirm the two promises landed. Moves straight to 'would that be said, I'll go ahead and send everything to you in an email.'
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Rep says 'if you need to make any changes just let us know' but never asks the genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or even 'any questions?'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Not asked. No version of 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' appears.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked. Rep does not ask 'Would you like our help with your move?' Booking is confirmed by default (it was already scheduled on Oct 29th); no explicit close for the business.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Not mentioned. No reference to rate-lock or holding the quote.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Confirmed: date (Oct 29), arrival window (8:45–9:15 AM), apartment numbers (4505 from, 2408 to). Missing: phone number confirmation, crew size, notes left for crew about concerns (couch/freight elevator complexity mentioned but not documented as crew notes).

top_strength: Joanna gathered comprehensive logistics details (walking distances, elevator access, couch freight-elevator requirement, new building unknowns) and anchored the estimate cleanly to the one-bedroom baseline plus walking-distance adjustments, landing on a transparent $900 quote with full fee disclosure.
coaching_note: This is a callback to an already-scheduled move, so the quid-pro-quo frame and explicit ask don't apply the same way — but the missing 'Does that feel fair?' pause before moving to confirmation, the absent final-concerns check, and the partial damage-coverage framing (no 'no deductible / no fine print' reassurance) left money and trust on the table; add a real pause after pricing and return to Section 6's genuine concern language even on rebook calls.
